title: Early nations
blurb: Writing, cities and pyramids appear. In Arabia, the nations of Ad and Thamud rise and are destroyed.

events.title: Writing begins
events.what: Sumerians in Uruk invent writing. Cities, kings and temples follow across Mesopotamia.
events.tie: The Quran swears by the pen and what people write (68:1), honouring the gift of writing that began in cities like these.

events.title: Egypt becomes one kingdom
events.what: Egypt is united under one king. Its rulers are later called Pharaohs, the title the Quran uses in Musa's story.
events.tie: Musa's story with Firaun is retold more often than any other in the Quran, which calls Egypt's king only by his title.

events.title: Caral, oldest city of the Americas
events.what: In Peru's Supe valley, people build pyramids and sunken plazas at Caral, the oldest known city in the Americas.
events.tie: The Quran often points to vanished nations 'greater in strength and in their marks on the land' (40:82).

events.title: The Great Pyramid
events.what: The Great Pyramid is built. It stays the tallest structure on earth for nearly 4,000 years.
events.tie: The Quran calls Firaun 'owner of the stakes' (89:10), a power built on monuments like these.

events.title: Cities of the Indus
events.what: The Indus Valley civilisation builds planned cities with drains and standard bricks.
events.tie: The Quran tells people to travel the land and see how earlier peoples ended (30:42); these cities lay forgotten for nearly four thousand years.

events.title: Stonehenge
events.what: Farmers in Britain raise giant stones in a circle lined up with the midsummer sunrise and the midwinter sunset.
events.tie: The Quran says Allah set the sun and moon in measured phases 'that you may know the number of years' (10:5).

events.title: The first empire
events.what: Sargon of Akkad unites Mesopotamia into the first known empire.
events.tie: The Quran tells of a Mesopotamian king who argued with Ibrahim 'because Allah had given him kingship' (2:258); tradition names him Namrud.

events.title: A monument on every height
events.what: The people of Ad build landmarks on every hill and strong fortresses, as if they will live forever. Hud asks them to fear Allah instead.

events.title: Hud and the people of Ad
events.what: Prophet Hud warns the mighty people of Ad in their city of pillars, Iram. They refuse. A screaming wind destroys them.

events.title: Empires fall in a great drought
events.what: A long drought strikes from Egypt to Iraq. The Akkadian empire falls and Egypt's Old Kingdom breaks apart.
events.tie: The Quran speaks of nations 'greater in power' who 'built up the earth', and still fell (30:9).

events.title: The horse is tamed
events.what: On the grasslands north of the Black Sea, people tame the horse that all riding horses descend from. Chariots soon spread across Asia and Europe.
events.tie: The Quran names horses, mules and donkeys as gifts 'for you to ride, and as adornment' (16:8).
events.note: Earlier taming at Botai in Kazakhstan, about 3500 BCE, was of a different line of horses.

events.title: Hud and the believers saved
events.what: Allah saves Hud and those who believed with him by His mercy. Tradition says Hud spent his last days in Hadramawt, where a shrine bears his name.
events.note: Some place his grave in Hadramawt, others in Makkah. Neither is certain.

events.title: The ziggurat of Ur
events.what: King Ur-Nammu builds a great stepped temple to the moon god Nanna and issues one of the oldest law codes.
events.tie: Tradition links Ur with Ibrahim, who would reject the worship of the setting moon (6:77).

events.title: The nine plotters
events.what: Nine men of mischief swear to kill Salih and his family by night. They plan, but Allah plans too, and their homes are left in ruins.

events.title: Salih and the she-camel
events.what: Thamud carve homes into the rock at al-Hijr. They kill the she-camel sent as a sign and are destroyed by a blast.

events.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh
events.what: Poems about Gilgamesh, king of Uruk, are written down. In later versions a man named Utnapishtim survives a great flood in a boat.
events.tie: The Quran's story of Nuh (11:25-48) is about one God, warning and repentance, where the epic tells of quarrelling gods.

events.title: Yu the Great and the Xia
events.what: Chinese tradition says Yu the Great tamed the floods and founded the Xia, China's first dynasty. Archaeologists debate whether Erlitou was its capital.
events.tie: The Quran says every nation was sent a messenger (16:36), though it names only some of them.

events.title: The Companions of al-Rass
events.what: The Quran names the Companions of al-Rass, 'the well', among nations destroyed for denying their messenger, beside Ad and Thamud.
events.note: Who they were is unknown. Commentators suggest a well in Najd, a town in Yamamah or a people by the Aras river; none is certain.

events.title: Hammurabi's law
events.what: Hammurabi rules Babylon and carves one of the oldest written law codes.
events.tie: Hammurabi's laws were carved in stone; the Quran says: 'Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct' (16:90).

events.title: Shang China
events.what: The Shang dynasty rules northern China. Oracle bones carry the earliest Chinese writing.
events.tie: Islam later reached China by sea and land, and millions of Chinese Muslims, like the Hui, still write in the script born on these bones.
